intro: Practice the job in your browser: log and prioritise a ticket in a service desk console, triage a queue, diagnose a PC that cannot reach the file server, and handle customer calls safely. Everything is graded for you.

labs.title: Log and prioritise an incident
labs.summary: Fill in a ticket in a service desk console: category, impact, urgency, priority and assignment.
labs.scenario: A call comes in. Maria Lopez (Finance) says the finance application shows an error and loops back to the login screen. Her whole department of 12 people has the same problem, and month-end close is due today. Nothing was changed by the team. Create the incident: set the right category, impact, urgency, priority and assignment, write a clear summary, then save.

fields.label: Notify the requester that the ticket is open

tasks.text: The requester is Maria Lopez and the category is Business application
The summary mentions the finance app and the login problem (for example "Finance application login loop, 12 users")
Impact is a department and urgency is high
Assigned to Application Support, and the requester is notified

hints: Twelve people are blocked: that is a department, not a single user. The deadline makes it urgent.
Impact department and urgency high gives P2 High. Only a company-wide outage would be P1.
A business application fault that Tier 1 cannot fix goes to Application Support (Tier 2).
labs.solution:
Requester: Maria Lopez
Category: Business application
Summary: Finance application login loop, 12 users, month-end close today
Impact: Department / several users
Urgency: High
Priority: P2 High
Assign to: Application Support (Tier 2)
Notify requester: on
labs.review: Priority comes from impact and urgency. A whole department blocked on a deadline is high priority, but not critical unless the entire company is affected. Always route to the team that can fix it and tell the requester the ticket exists.

labs.title: Triage the queue
labs.summary: Prioritise tickets, put troubleshooting steps in order, and fill in key help desk terms.
labs.scenario: Six tickets arrived at the same time. Decide which to handle first, and show that you know the standard troubleshooting order.

activities.title: Set the priority
activities.prompt: Match each ticket to a priority.

items.text: Email is down for the whole company
The sales team cannot reach the CRM during a quarter-end push
One user's laptop will not connect to Wi-Fi
A user asks for a second monitor
The payment system is offline and customers cannot buy
A shared printer on the 3rd floor is out of toner

activities.title: The troubleshooting steps
activities.prompt: Put the troubleshooting steps in order.
items: Establish a theory of probable cause

rows.label: What does SLA stand for? (three words)
Which tier usually takes the first contact? (number)
Impact and ___ decide a ticket's priority

tasks.text: Assign the right priority to each ticket

hints: Count how many people and how much of the business each issue affects, then how urgent it is.
It starts with gathering facts and ends with writing it down.
SLA: how fast you must respond and resolve.
labs.review: Whole-company or revenue-stopping issues are critical. A blocked team on a deadline is high. One user is medium, and convenience requests are low. Then follow the method every time: identify, theory, test, fix, verify, document.

labs.title: Diagnose "I can't open the file server"
labs.summary: Use ipconfig, ping and nslookup to separate network from name-resolution problems, then fix the DNS setting.
labs.scenario:
Priya (HR) says she can no longer open FILES01. Web pages by name also fail, but her Wi-Fi shows connected. You are on her PC, HR-PC12 (command prompt). Work through the layers, then fix it:

  • Check the IP configuration
  • Prove the local network works by pinging the gateway 10.30.0.1
  • Test name resolution with nslookup
  • Correct the DNS server (the company DNS is 10.30.0.5) and verify FILES01 responds

options: The PC points at a DNS server that no longer answers

hints: If pinging the gateway works, the local network is fine, so look higher up.
nslookup files01 times out when the DNS server is unreachable or not answering.
netsh interface ip set dns name="Ethernet" static 10.30.0.5
labs.solution:
ipconfig /all
ping 10.30.0.1
nslookup files01
netsh interface ip set dns name="Ethernet" static 10.30.0.5
nslookup files01
ping files01
labs.review: Work from the bottom up: address, gateway, then names. Gateway pings fine but names fail: it is DNS. Fix the cause, verify the original complaint, then write it up.

labs.title: Customer scenarios
labs.summary: Choose helpful phrases, handle an upset caller in order, and spot a social engineering attempt.
labs.scenario: You are on the phones. Show you can talk to people the way a good support technician does.

activities.title: What is this phrase doing?
activities.prompt: Match each phrase to its purpose.

items.text: I understand how frustrating this is with a deadline.
I'll call you back by 3 pm with an update.
So the printer shows offline since this morning. Is that right?
You should have read the email we sent.
That sounds stressful, let's get you working again.

activities.title: An upset caller
activities.prompt: Put the steps for handling an upset customer in order.
items: Stay calm and let them explain
Say what you will do now
Follow up and confirm it is fixed

rows.label: A caller says they are the CEO, in a rush, and demands a password reset without verification. Which social-engineering red flag is this? (one word: pressure or urgency)
Before resetting an account you must first ___ the caller's identity
Should a technician ever ask a user to read out their password? (yes/no)

tasks.text: Match the phrases to their purpose
Order the steps for an upset caller

hints: Empathy names the feeling; expectations give a time; confirming repeats back; blaming points at the user.
Calm first, solution last, and a follow-up to close.
Pressure and urgency are classic tricks.
labs.review: Listen, acknowledge, act, set a time and follow up. And verify before you reset: urgency and authority are exactly how attackers get through a help desk.
